Going on a picnic can be a lot of fun. Especially when you are getting all your friends together at one place to enjoy some tasty bites and good laughter. Whether you decide to take a lot of things or just go there with a few items it won’t matter. What matters is that you all have a good time regardless of what you take or not take. There are certain essentials that we think will make your picnic a tad bit more fun. Travelling on a bike means that you might be limited in the things you can take, but that should not keep you from having a good time. If you can make the effort to carry a few things you are bound to have a good time. Here are a few items we think will make for a good picnic.

Foot Gear to Help You

First and foremost you will have to make sure you wear a good pair of motorbike boots. These should give you enough traction so that you can manage any walking once you have reached the destination. They also have to be comfortable enough to allow you to ride the distance in a comfortable manner. Wearing breathable socks is a must. This way you will have feet that are not sweaty and wet. The socks should be able to wick away the sweat from your feet. If the shoes have enough insole padding it will provide your feet with the much needed comfort and support when walking around in stony and uneven ground. So select something that is of good quality and make sure you are putting your money to good use by getting something that is going to last you for long. There is no point in spending money in something that looks fancy but doesn’t offer the needed support.

Some Sort of Resting Equipment

You could take some camp chairs that are built for such occasions. They come in such a manner that you can take them on your bike with ease. These are a great option especially of if you want to sit comfortably. The place can be rocky and sitting on stones can be uncomfortable especially with all your bike gear on. So grab some camp chairs and make sure you have somewhere to sit comfortably. You could carry picnic blankets but they might not be the best for the biker family.

Pack Plenty of Food

Maybe travelling on a bike is not the same as a car thus limiting you when it comes to the amount of things to take. But you need to pack wisely so that you will have plenty of food and water. Youwon’t be able to find much at your point of destination, unless it’s a well-known spot with kiosks set up. As long as you have enough water and some energy providing snacks you should be fine for the road.

Make sure you plan and organize well with your crew before you set off. This way you can be sure that you have not left anything behind.
